prompt: Stage 4-2, level 8, 53 gold, 41 HP on a 3-loss streak. You took the augment and levelled at 4-1; the planned rolldown is 4-5. Aphelios is 1-star with Rageblade, Infinity Edge and Last Whisper and you hold a second copy on the bench. The shop shows a third. Buying him drops you to 49. Scouting says the next opponent beats your current board by two units. What do you do?

options.label: Buy him, put the 2-star in, and stop: 49 gold, hold to 4-5
Lock the shop and buy him at 4-3 so you collect the full 5 interest first
Buy him and roll down to 30 while you are under 50 anyway; the rolldown is just three rounds early

explanation:
The floor exists to make you arrive at your rolldown with the most gold. It is not a rule about the number 50. Here the arithmetic is one gold: at 49 you earn 4 interest at 4-3 instead of 5, and with base income you are back at 58 before 4-4. Against that one gold, the third copy turns a 1-star carry with three items into a 2-star, which is the difference between losing by two units and winning the 4-2 fight. Stage 4 losses cost 12 to 15 HP; at 41 you have three of them before stage 5, where one loss is 20. A 2-star carry now saves more HP in one fight than the interest earns in a whole stage.

Locking the shop keeps the copy safe and keeps the 1 gold, and pays 12 to 15 HP for it. Rolling to 30 is the opposite error: 4-2 is not your rolldown, the tank is already 2-star, and 20 gold spent at 4-2 is 20 gold missing at 4-5 when the shop actually has to deliver.
principle: One gold of interest is never worth a fight. Break the floor for the copy that changes the fight, then hold.
commonMistake: Locking the shop or skipping the copy to protect the number 50 when the missing interest is one gold and the fight is worth 12 HP.
hint: Work out exactly how much interest 49 gold loses at 4-3, then compare it with what one stage-4 loss costs in HP.
